/-!
# Conjecture 5.5

by B. A. F. Wehrfritz

If $G$ is a finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite group, does there exist a
finitely generated metabelian group $M$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of the
automorphism group of $M$? If so, many of the tricky properties of $G$ like its residual
finiteness would become transparent.

Here a group is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ with all factors
$G_{i+1}/G_i$ cyclic, and it is *metabelian* if its commutator subgroup is abelian. For classes
of groups $\mathfrak{X}$ and $\mathfrak{Y}$, a group is $\mathfrak{X}$-by-$\mathfrak{Y}$ if it
has a normal subgroup in $\mathfrak{X}$ with quotient in $\mathfrak{Y}$. Thus $G$ is
abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite if it has an abelian normal subgroup $A$ such that $G/A$ has a
polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def IsPolycyclicOfLength : ℕ → (G : Type*) → [Group G] → Prop
  | 0, G, _ => Subsingleton G
  | n + 1, G, _ =>
    ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal), IsPolycyclicOfLength n N ∧ IsCyclic (G ⧸ N)
blocks.docstring:
`IsPolycyclicOfLength n G` means that `G` has a subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ of length $n$ in
which every factor $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is cyclic. It is defined by recursion on $n$: a series of length
$0$ exists exactly when $G$ is trivial, and a series of length $n + 1$ exists exactly when $G$
has a normal subgroup $N$ with $G/N$ cyclic and $N$ having such a series of length $n$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsSolvable`/`derivedSeries` (too weak: solvable ≠ polycyclic), `CompositionSeries`/`RelSeries` (JordanHolder-style maximal series, not cyclic-factor subnormal series), `IsCyclic` (used for the factors).
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.5».IsPolycyclicOfLength
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a subnormal series with cyclic factors. Defined by recursion on the length n: length 0 ⇔ `Subsingleton G`; length n+1 ⇔ ∃ normal N with `IsPolycyclicOfLength n N ∧ IsCyclic (G ⧸ N)`. This is exactly a series 1 = G_0 ⊴ … ⊴ G_n = G with cyclic factors, peeled from the top.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question with an implicit universal quantifier over all G (∀ G f.g. with an abelian normal subgroup A such that G/A has a polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index, ∃ f.g. metabelian M and an injective group hom G → MulAut M); 'X-by-Y' means a normal subgroup in X with quotient in Y, 'metabelian' means derived length ≤ 2 (commutator subgroup abelian), and 'polycyclic' (subnormal series with cyclic factors) and 'metabelian' have no Mathlib definitions so bespoke ones are needed; the final sentence 'If so, many of the tricky properties ... would become transparent' is motivation, not a further question.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates compile and state the same faithful content: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ f.g. group G with an abelian normal A such that G/A has a polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index, ∃ f.g. metabelian M and an injective hom G →* MulAut M. c02 was chosen for quality: clear recursive definition of polycyclic (length-n cyclic subnormal series, base case = trivial group), explicit IsPolycyclicByFinite and IsMetabelian (commutator subgroup abelian), full docstrings, and five proven API tests including IsMetabelian G ↔ derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥, which confirms the bespoke notion matches 'derived length ≤ 2'. Shipped verbatim; compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.5

by B. A. F. Wehrfritz

If $G$ is a finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite group, does there exist a
finitely generated metabelian group $M$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of the
automorphism group of $M$? If so, many of the tricky properties of $G$ like its residual
finiteness would become transparent.

Here a group is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ with all factors
$G_{i+1}/G_i$ cyclic, and it is *metabelian* if its commutator subgroup is abelian. For classes
of groups $\mathfrak{X}$ and $\mathfrak{Y}$, a group is $\mathfrak{X}$-by-$\mathfrak{Y}$ if it
has a normal subgroup in $\mathfrak{X}$ with quotient in $\mathfrak{Y}$. Thus $G$ is
abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite if it has an abelian normal subgroup $A$ such that $G/A$ has a
polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.5»

/-- `IsPolycyclicOfLength n G` means that `G` has a subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ of length $n$ in
which every factor $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is cyclic. It is defined by recursion on $n$: a series of length
$0$ exists exactly when $G$ is trivial, and a series of length $n + 1$ exists exactly when $G$
has a normal subgroup $N$ with $G/N$ cyclic and $N$ having such a series of length $n$. -/
def IsPolycyclicOfLength : ℕ → (G : Type*) → [Group G] → Prop
  | 0, G, _ => Subsingleton G
  | n + 1, G, _ =>
    ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal), IsPolycyclicOfLength n N ∧ IsCyclic (G ⧸ N)

/-- A group is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series with cyclic factors. -/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n, IsPolycyclicOfLength n G

/-- A group is *polycyclic-by-finite* if it has a polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index. -/
def IsPolycyclicByFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (P : Subgroup G) (_ : P.Normal), IsPolycyclic P ∧ P.FiniteIndex

/-- A group is *metabelian* if its commutator subgroup is abelian, i.e. it has derived length at
most $2$. -/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsMulCommutative (commutator G)

/-- The trivial group is polycyclic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolycyclic_of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] : IsPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨0, (inferInstance : Subsingleton G)⟩

/-- Every cyclic group is polycyclic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolycyclic_of_isCyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsCyclic G] : IsPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨1, ⊥, inferInstance, (inferInstance : Subsingleton (⊥ : Subgroup G)),
    isCyclic_of_surjective (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).symm
      (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).symm.surjective⟩

/-- Every finite group is polycyclic-by-finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolycyclicByFinite_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsPolycyclicByFinite G :=
  ⟨⊥, inferInstance, isPolycyclic_of_subsingleton _, inferInstance⟩

/-- Every abelian group is metabelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsMetabelian G :=
  inferInstanceAs (IsMulCommutative (commutator G))

/-- A group is metabelian if and only if its derived length is at most $2$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_iff_derivedSeries_two_eq_bot (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    IsMetabelian G ↔ derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥ := by
  rw [IsMetabelian, derivedSeries_succ, derivedSeries_one,
    Subgroup.commutator_eq_bot_iff_le_centralizer, Subgroup.le_centralizer_iff_isMulCommutative]

/--
If $G$ is a finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite group, does there exist a
finitely generated metabelian group $M$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of the
automorphism group of $M$?

Here $G$ is abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite if it has an abelian normal subgroup $A$ such that
$G/A$ has a polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index. "$G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of
$\operatorname{Aut}(M)$" is stated as the existence of an injective group homomorphism
$G \to \operatorname{Aut}(M)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.FG G],
      (∃ (A : Subgroup G) (_ : A.Normal),
        IsMulCommutative A ∧ IsPolycyclicByFinite (G ⧸ A)) →
      ∃ (M : Type) (_ : Group M), Group.FG M ∧ IsMetabelian M ∧
        ∃ φ : G →* MulAut M, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.5»

items: 'abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite' is read as abelian-by-(polycyclic-by-finite), as in the decomposition table: an abelian normal subgroup A with G/A having a polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index. (The other bracketing, (abelian-by-polycyclic)-by-finite, defines the same class of groups: given N ⊴ G of finite index with abelian A ⊴ N and N/A polycyclic, the intersection of the finitely many G-conjugates of A is an abelian normal subgroup of G with the required quotient; the converse is immediate.)
'G is isomorphic to a subgroup of Aut(M)' is formalized as `∃ φ : G →* MulAut M, Function.Injective φ`; `MulAut M` is Mathlib's group of multiplicative (i.e. group) automorphisms of M.

Both G and M are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the repository's Kourovka idiom. This loses no generality: finitely generated groups are countable, hence isomorphic to groups in `Type`.
'Finitely generated' is `Group.FG`. 'Finite index' is `Subgroup.FiniteIndex` (index ≠ 0). 'Abelian normal subgroup' is `A.Normal` with `IsMulCommutative A`.
`IsCyclic` in Mathlib includes the trivial group and infinite cyclic groups, matching the usual definition of polycyclic (factors may be finite or infinite cyclic, possibly trivial).

The hypotheses of the ∀ are placed after the quantified G as an implication (`(∃ A …) → ∃ M …`), avoiding the `∃ x, P x → Q` pitfall; the hypothesis is satisfiable (e.g. G = ℤ), so the statement is not vacuous.
The final sentence of the problem ('If so, many of the tricky properties…') is motivation and appears only in the module docstring, not in the formal statement.

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; no candidate omitted anything and none raised decomposition objections. Modeling points verified: (1) 'abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite' is bracketed as abelian-by-(polycyclic-by-finite); the other bracketing gives the same class (take the core of the abelian normal subgroup of the finite-index normal subgroup), so no generality is lost. (2) Requiring the finite-index polycyclic subgroup to be normal is equivalent to merely having one, since polycyclic groups are subgroup-closed and finite-index subgroups have finite-index normal cores. (3) Mathlib's IsCyclic includes trivial and infinite cyclic groups, as required for polycyclic series factors. (4) 'G isomorphic to a subgroup of Aut(M)' = injective G →* MulAut M. (5) G, M : Type is harmless since f.g. groups are countable. (6) Hypothesis is satisfiable (e.g. G = ℤ), and the ∀-with-implication form avoids the ∃x, P x → Q pitfall. The closing sentence of the source ('If so, many of the tricky properties ... transparent') is motivation and is only reproduced in the module docstring. Differences among candidates (Fin-indexed vs recursive vs inductive polycyclic series; FiniteIndex vs Finite quotient; IsMulCommutative (commutator G) vs derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥) are all provably equivalent, so no candidate is unfaithful.
